newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian parliament begins debate on new cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian parliament begins debate on new cabinet.

text.p: The Slovenian parliament began a debate on Thursday on a new cabinet proposed by prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek and was expected to vote on whether to approve it later in the day.

"The government is balanced...and will try to reach basic strategic goals like membership of European organisations and NATO, improved economic competitiveness, better economic results and the balanced development of Slovenia," Drnovsek told the assembly.

Drnovsek, of the centre-left Liberal Democrats, last week announced he had formed a coalition with the conservative People's Party and pensioners' party Desus, over three months after an inconclusive November 10 general election.
The coalition holds 49 out of 90 parliamentary seats. Two representatives of Hungarian and Italian minorities and an independent deputy are also expected to give their backing to the line-up.
"It would be quite a surprise if the government is not confirmed, but in politics anything can happen," a political analyst said.
But all the opposition parties said they would not support the new cabinet.

"Slovenia needs a government, but not a government of Janez Drnovsek, who should have returned his mandate after the first unsuccessful vote (of his previous cabinet)," said Miroslav Mozetic, head of the Christian Democrat parliamentary group .

Drnovsek's first line-up, formed in coalition with the United List of Social Democrats, the Nationalist Party and the Pensioners' Party Desus, was rejected three weeks ago by an even vote of 45 to 45.

"The Social Democrats regret what is about to happen here today -- because this was brought about by breaching a lot of moral values," said Ivo Hvalica, head of the parliamentary group of the Social Democrats.

The Christian Democrats and the Social Democrats said the decision of the People's Party to leave the so-called "Spring" alliance, which comprised the three parties, and join Drnovsek's government, was "immoral".
"I hope the government will be approved as there is no alternative at the moment. The only alternative is early election," Marjan Podobnik, head of the People's Party, told Radio Slovenija.

If the parliament fails to approve at least two-thirds of the cabinet, in which the Liberal Democrats and the People's Party each have nine posts, and Desus one, President Milan Kucan has to nominate a new prime minister.
The new government if approved will be the third since Slovenia's independence from the former Yugoslavia in 1991.
Drnovsek has been acting prime minister since April 1992.
The new government is the third since Slovenia gained independence from the former Yugoslavia in 1991. Drnovsek of the Liberal Democrats has been acting prime minister since April 1992.
The vote was 52 against 37 in favour of Drnovsek's cabinet line-up.
Drnovsek last week formed a coalition with the conservative People's Party and the pensioners' party Desus, over three months after an inconclusive November 10 general election.

Drnovsek's first attempt to form a government in coalition with the United List of Social Democrats, the Nationalist Party and Desus was rejected by parliament three weeks ago by an even vote of 45 to 45.
